note: Titumir as leader of the Wahabi movement: neither Titumir nor the Wahabi movement is named in any fetched source (NCERT lehs301/hess203/hess204; IGNOU BHIC-110 Unit 13; IGNOU Tribal Movements Unit 1). Source gap; disclosed in the faraizi_mappila exam_note. The chapter teaches the contemporary Faraizi movement of Bengal instead.
Indigo Rebellion immediately after 1857: hess203 dates the refusal to grow indigo to March 1859 (c31), right after the 1857 revolt (HIS-19).

Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-24). The chapter teaches the Mappila uprisings of 1836-54 in Malabar (BHIC-110 Unit 13, §13.3.7), but the 1921 Moplah rebellion itself is not in the fetched sources. Partial background only.
Birsa, leader of the Munda rebellion (Ulgulan): hess204 and IGNOU Unit 1 teach Birsa's movement in full (c42, c45-c48).
Sidhu and Kanu are associated with the Santhal revolt (c24; IGNOU Unit 1 §1.4.3 and lehs301).
Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-16). Dewan Velu Thampi's Travancore rebellion is not in any fetched source. Source gap.
Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-13). The Satnami rebellion (Aurangzeb's reign) is a Mughal-era topic, not in this chapter's fetched sources. Source gap.

Neel Darpan's author (Dinabandhu Mitra): the indigo revolt is taught in full, but neither the play nor its author is named in the fetched sources (hess203 mentions only unnamed Calcutta intellectuals writing on the ryots' misery). Source gap; disclosed in the indigo_deccan exam_note. [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]
Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-20). Editor of the Hindoo Patriot (Harish Chandra Mukherjee): press history, not in the fetched sources. Source gap.

Neel Darpan as the book depicting the plight of indigo cultivators: same gap as 2017 Q97 — the play is not named in the fetched sources. The indigo system and revolt themselves are taught (c29-c34). [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]
Kuka movement is associated with Punjab: the Kuka/Namdhari movement is not mentioned in any fetched source. Source gap; named in the faraizi_mappila exam_note. [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]
'Ulgulan' is associated with the Munda uprising: Birsa's Munda movement is taught in full (c42-c48); the section flags that exam questions call this movement 'Ulgulan'.
Titumir's original name (Syed Mir Nasar Ali): Titumir is not named in any fetched source. Source gap (see 2015 Q55).
Sidho and Kanho are associated with the Santhal rebellion (c24).

Hero of the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24 (Alluri Sitarama Raju): IGNOU Unit 1 names 'the Rampa rebellion of Alluri Sitaram, which was also directed against the forest rules' (c54). The exact years 1922-24 are not in the source; the leader identification is taught.

Alt for HIS-24 as well. The Eka movement (a peasant movement, Awadh 1921) is not covered in any fetched source — NCERT Class X Nationalism in India (jess302) could not be fetched in this run and no IGNOU unit used covers Eka. Source gap. [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]
Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-25, ONE_AS_ALT). Who gave Gaidinliu the title 'Rani' (Nehru): not in any fetched source. Source gap.
Faraizi movement in Bengal was started by Haji Shariatullah (c12; BHIC-110 Unit 13, §13.3.6).
Leader of the Eka movement (Madari Pasi): Eka is not covered in the fetched sources (see 2021 Q47). Source gap. [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]

Leader of the Tana Bhagat movement: the movement itself is taught — among the Oraons of Chotanagpur the Bhagat movement was called the Tana Bhagat movement (c52) — but the leader's name (Jatra Oraon) appears in no fetched source. Partial: movement taught, leader name is a source gap. [Taught after 19 Nov 2026 extension.]

Tribal leader regarded as an incarnation of God / Dharti Aba (Birsa Munda): hess204 records that thousands followed Birsa believing he was bhagwan (God) and that God had appointed him (section birsa_later). The specific title 'Dharti Aba' is not in the sources; the identification is unambiguous from what is taught.

Leader of the Kherwar or Safa Hor movement (Bhagirath Manjhi): IGNOU Unit 1 names Bhagirath Manjhi ('Babaji') as leader of the Kherwar movement of the Santhals (c51) and records Sapha Hor as the Santhals' Bhagat movement (c53).
Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-26, ONE_AS_ALT). Leader of the Reang uprising in Tripura 1942-43 (Ratan Mani): not in any fetched source. Source gap.

Alt-mapping only (primary HIS-17). Bengal Tenancy Act 1885: the Act is not in the fetched sources, and the Pabna agrarian movement that forms its usual background is likewise absent from NCERT/IGNOU texts fetched. Source gap.
